propositions: The compaction sweep spawns one git log --full-history walk per ticket inside the store write lock, each at ~100% CPU, holding the global write lock for minutes and stalling all writers
Per-ticket history walk misses fall through to per-event wildcard pathspec walks ('*<event-id>*.json'), each a full-history scan, worse than the intended per-ticket cost
_commit_backfill stages with unscoped 'git add -A', allowing concurrent writer in-flight event files to be committed under the compaction message
The sweep never re-yields: compact_all_cli loops through all tickets without re-probing write_lock_is_busy, so writers arriving after sweep start wait for the entire run to complete
Hoisting the history walk to a single position-keyed map built before any lock is acquired, plus scoped staging and mid-run re-yield, moves git-log cost out of the critical section
The position-keyed map builder (build_position_commit_map) is the correct primitive; a path-keyed sibling (build_introducing_commit_map) would miss every lookup and silently restore per-event walks
